toegepas.na: wat so 'n gebruik in daardie gemeenskap beteken
toegepas.rede_vinder: 'daar' is vague, since no place has been named in the sentence before it; it means the other community.
toegepas.fout: 'daar' could be read as the house named just before it rather than the other community.
toegepas.rede_keurder: Naming 'daardie gemeenskap' removes the ambiguity without moving the meaning, and matches the lesson's own place-time-community framing.

laat_vaar.voor: Hier is dit eers vrolik en word dit gespanne
laat_vaar.na: Hier is die stemming eers vrolik, en dit word gespanne
laat_vaar.rede_vinder: 'dit' could point back to the drama rather than the mood; naming 'stemming' makes the reference clear, and the AWS comma goes before 'en' joining two full clauses.
laat_vaar.rede_keurder: The previous sentence makes 'stemming' its subject, so 'dit' already points to the mood, and the shared-subject clause needs no comma; the proposal is longer without being clearly better.

laat_vaar.voor: laat voel jy is op 'n plaas
laat_vaar.na: laat voel dat jy op 'n plaas is
laat_vaar.rede_vinder: In written Afrikaans the dependent clause after 'laat voel' reads better with 'dat' and the verb at the end.
laat_vaar.rede_keurder: 'laat voel jy is op 'n plaas' is natural, plain Afrikaans; adding 'dat' only makes it more formal, a lateral move.

laat_vaar.voor: as jy dink almal in sy groep is net soos hy
laat_vaar.na: as jy dink dat almal in sy groep net soos hy is
laat_vaar.rede_vinder: In written text the subordinate clause after 'dink' reads better with 'dat' and the verb at the end.
laat_vaar.rede_keurder: Leaving out 'dat' after 'dink' is normal Afrikaans and the sentence reads easily for a Grade 5 learner; the change is lateral.

laat_vaar.rede_vinder: Repeating the article keeps the two choices parallel, as the lesson does elsewhere ('n dans of 'n drama).
laat_vaar.rede_keurder: 'n drama of dans' is an acceptable, smooth pairing; repeating the article only reads differently.

na_skrywer.voor: 'n gesig of ding van baie naby
na_skrywer.na: 'n gesig of 'n ding van baie naby
na_skrywer.rede_vinder: Repeating the article keeps the two nouns parallel and reads more naturally.
na_skrywer.fout: The bare 'ding' without an article reads clipped in the definition.
na_skrywer.rede_keurder: This is a glossary definition and the change goes beyond a plain spelling or grammar error, so it goes to the writer as a flag rather than being applied.
na_skrywer.waarom: the reviewer sent it to the writer

laat_vaar_vorige.rede_vinder: 'Daarom ... daar' doubles the reference to the radio drama and reads clumsily; 'Daarom' already carries it, and a word is saved.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_keurder: 'Daar' ties the sound effects to the radio drama; without it the sentence reads as a general claim, so information is lost and the original reads acceptably.

laat_vaar_vorige.rede_vinder: 'maar nie vir 'n kultuur nie' has no subject and verb of its own and joins a command, so under AWS 2017 it takes no comma.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_keurder: A contrastive comma before 'maar' is normal Afrikaans practice and helps the Grade 5 reader; the never-a-comma rule applies to 'en', so removing it is not an improvement.

laat_vaar_vorige.rede_vinder: 'Met oefen' uses a bare verb as a noun after a preposition; 'deur oefening' is the correct and natural form, same word count.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_keurder: The preposition change moves the meaning from what changed while they rehearsed to what changed because of rehearsing, and 'met oefen' is acceptable Afrikaans.

laat_vaar_vorige.na: om jammer te sê is moeilik
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_vinder: A verb phrase used as subject takes the 'om ... te' infinitive in standard Afrikaans.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_keurder: A bare verbal phrase as subject ('jammer sê is moeilik') is correct, natural Afrikaans, like 'swem is lekker', so the om-te form is only a more formal alternative.

laat_vaar_vorige.voor: Lag gerus saam met 'n grappige oomblik
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_vinder: 'Saam met' is used with people, not moments (calque of 'laugh with'); 'lag vir' is idiomatic and keeps the contrast with 'nie vir 'n kultuur nie'.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_keurder: The preposition carries the point: 'saam met' means laughing along with the moment and 'vir' means laughing at, so the swap erases the with/at contrast the sentence is built on.
